translations: Aman sat on a rocky outcropping thirty feet from the shore, furiously scribbling away with his brush. When he heard the commotion, his hand shook, and the ink splattered, forming a half-finished "R" in the character. He quickly blew on the ink, but a droplet of saliva landed on the bamboo slip, and he frantically wiped it away with his sleeve, only to smudge the previous line, "The Dragon Palace trembles." A nearby fisherman, carrying a wicker basket, caught sight of Aman's disheveled state and chuckled, "What's the big deal?" Aman stuck out his neck, "I'm writing about the Night Demon's first appearance!" The fisherman pointed at Aman's shiny forehead, "What's so dignified about that? Looks like you've got a grease slick!"

Nezha clearly heard the exchange, and his steel trident spun around, pointing at the fisherman, "Mind your own business!" Nezha stepped forward, his smile still plastered on his face, but his feet firmly planted on the ground. "You're looking for me, not some bystander trying to flex your muscles." The fisherman didn't back down, but instead, he picked up his wicker basket and started to walk away, passing by Aman and giving him a quick tug on the back of his neck, pulling him off the slippery rock. Aman's feet flailed wildly on the ground, "Wait! A historian's dignity needs to be respected!" The fisherman retorted, "You worry about your own posterior!"

Nezha didn't immediately counterattack. Instead, he tied one end of the Red Silk to his wrist and let the other end dangle into the water. Nezha sidestepped the trident, and the red fabric flowed into the water, wrapping around the trident's tip. However, he didn't exert any force. Nezha thought Li Jing believed him to be weak, so he waited for the trident to strike again. When Li Jing tried to pull back, Nezha suddenly released the silk, and Li Jing's trident was caught off guard, causing him to stumble and his back foot to sink into the mud, creating a half-foot-deep trench. Nezha looked down at the trench and said, "If you came to help the fishermen dig a drainage ditch, you're off by a bit."

A burst of laughter echoed from the shore, followed by an awkward silence. Li Jing's anger boiled over, and he spun around, using the momentum to swing his trident. Nezha ducked under the trident, his knees scraping against the water's surface, sending a string of water droplets flying. As he quickly stood up, his wet hair clung to his face, temporarily blinding him. He tilted his head back, relying on the wind to guide him. The trident's tip whizzed past his nose, and Nezha hastily pushed his hair behind his ear, still refusing to back down, "Wait, the sea breeze is playing tricks on me, and you're using my hair to blind me!" Li Jing retorted, "In a battle to the death, who has time to worry about hair?"

"Not me, then." Nezha's words were barely out when the K'unlun Circle flew out from under his hair, hitting the trident's handle and then returning to his hand. This time, Nezha saw the full force of Li Jing's attack and noticed that the civilians had retreated to a safe distance. Aman didn't intervene, nor did he move closer, but instead, he pressed the green bamboo slips against his knee and rapidly wrote two lines: "Li Jing attacks, Nezha dodges; Li Jing presses forward, Nezha counterattacks." By the time he looked up, the two warriors' weapons had clashed for the third time, sending sparks flying.

Li Jing thrust his trident forward, "You impudent little brat, disregarding the rules!" Nezha dodged the trident's tip and pulled out the K'unlun Circle with his right hand. "You won't play by the rules, so I'll show you my strength." Nezha said, and with a flick of his wrist, the K'unlun Circle sliced through the water, striking Li Jing's shoulder armor. Li Jing stumbled backward, his feet slipping in the mud, and he fell into the shallow bay. He struggled to raise his trident, but the Red Silk had wrapped around the handle, pulling it away. The K'unlun Circle flew back, striking Li Jing's chest. Li Jing lay motionless on the beach, and Nezha bent down to check his pulse, his smile fading.

Li Jing's trident left a silver streak on the water's surface, as if the K'unlun Circle had "washed white" it. Nezha looked out at the Nine Bays River, where the water grass swayed in the wind, like a silent commentary on the conflict. Aman lifted his pen, and the ink swirled in the air, as if he wanted to turn this scene into a painting, but Nezha's gaze froze the pen, and it stopped moving.

"Hey, Nezha, stop treating the K'unlun Circle like a toy!" Li Jing shouted from the shore, his voice tinged with resignation. Nezha covered his mouth with his hand, but his lips still twitched, as if he was trying to stifle a smile. Aman looked up and saw Nezha's "tough guy" expression, and he couldn't help but think to himself, "This kid's got guts, he's a real hard nut."

Li Jing's body rolled in the water, like a wave washing over him, and eventually, he sank quietly to the bottom. Nezha's fingers gently stroked the K'unlun Circle, feeling its temperature, as if it was reminding him that power was not absolute. Aman pressed the pen tip to the bamboo slip, and the ink slowly spread, like this conflict was being written into history.

Nezha's gaze shifted from the water to the shore, where Li Jing and his wife were holding hands, their faces etched with worry. Nezha bowed his head, taking a deep breath, as if he was telling himself, "I shouldn't have worried my parents and the people." He lifted his hand, and the K'unlun Circle spun gently in the air, like a soft glow had been added to this memory.
